Article Title: Prevent misuse of data by private entities, SC tells government
Article Text:
SC flags private access to sensitive PF, I-T data, asks Centre to prevent misuse by firms

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday expressed concern about a commercial technological ecosystem which allegedly accesses, retrieves and verifies sensitive individual information on provident fund and income tax returns and told the Centre about the desirability of devising an antidote to the problem with the assistance of domain experts.Hearing a PIL by Piyush Sharma, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana noted the matter essentially fell within policy domain but termed private access to sovereign data - individual information given to govt under legislative mandate - and its commercial exploitation as worrisome.Petitioner said his personal inquiry into the issue had revealed that "upon merely furnishing PAN and UAN details to a private verification workflow, the petitioner received complete employment history corresponding the said identifiers. No OTP authentication was generated. No explicit consent was obtained. No visible authorisation-based identity verification process was undertaken".Without blaming govt agencies for any leakage of data, the petitioner highlighted the insecure status of individual data given to govt under the mandate of different laws, as they are accessed at will by private entities."Despite the statutory architecture governing EPFO and I-T data, there appears to be an emerging and concerning pattern wherein private employment verification ecosystems rely upon data corresponding to statutory employment and financial records for purposes such as employment verification, moonlighting detection, dual employment screening, labour market profiling and employment decision-making," he said.SC agreed it was a serious matter but said it must be dealt with through a policy decision. On learning the petitioner sent two comprehensive representations on the issues to Centre, it asked govt to take "necessary steps to prevent misuse of individual data by private enterprises."
Article Summary: Sc flags private access to sensitive pf, i-t data, asks centre to prevent misuse by firms. Petitioner said his personal inquiry into the issue had revealed that "upon merely furnishing pan and uan details to a private verification workflow, the petitioner received complete employment history corresponding the said identifiers"

Article Title: Scientists stuck in red tape and admin work: Niti Aayog report
Article Text:
The report called for more trust-based, outcome-oriented governance model

The problem begins with money. India spends 0.6% of its GDP on R&D, a constant for over a decade.

BENGALURU: India may be producing more research papers, patents and startups, but scientists are still spending too much time navigating the system meant to support their work.A new NITI Aayog report on the Ease of Doing Research & Development lists procedural problems researchers face, from repeated grant applications and delayed funds to cumbersome procurement, vacant posts and excessive administrative controls.The report says India’s R&D ecosystem is still marked by a “significant trust deficit between the R&D project granting agency and researchers”, which keeps scientists from utilising their time purely for research.“Researchers are often not able to utilise their time purely for R&D activities without being worried about the administrative issues. There are also issues of capacity as well as rigidities in the science administration systems, which are largely internal to the institutions,” the report reads.The problem begins with money. India spends 0.6% of its GDP on R&D, a constant for over a decade. Competition for grants has intensified too, with the application-to-grant ratio falling below 10% at several agencies, while 64% of India’s R&D spending comes from the public sector, pointing to weak private participation.Even approved projects wait. Release of a sanctioned grant can take 3-6 months after the scientific decision, pushing overall turnaround to a year or more. Funds are also withdrawn at year-end and reassigned later, disrupting projects and fellowship payments.Human resources are another weak point. India has just 262 full-time equivalent researchers per million people, against 1,585 in China and 4,821 in both the US and UK. The postdoctoral ecosystem is thin, with only about 2,500 fellowships supported annually, and a PhD scholar’s first instalment can take 4-5 months. Sanctioned posts often stay vacant, with institutions unable to redeploy them where needed.Inside institutions, scientists often do jobs that should belong to professional research administrators, since many lack dedicated R&D offices and keep approvals centralised. India does well in publications and patents, but weak technology-transfer infrastructure limits their conversion into products — a burden felt hardest outside premier institutions, which face high journal costs and heavy teaching loads.The report flags a funding concentration problem. “...For instance, the IIT system is known to receive more than 80% of ANRF’s R&D funding. While uniformity in R&D funding is neither expected nor desirable, over-concentration of funding in only a selected set of institutions reduces the funding opportunity for researchers working in other R&D institutions and HEIs. It may be noted that ANRF has a specific mandate for supporting R&D in state institutions, however, this goal is far from being achieved,” it reads.Prof Jayanth Murthy, former director of the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, said money isn’t the biggest hurdle. PhD stipends, he pointed out, are fully budgeted and yet routinely delayed for no reason: “The money is committed, but you’re not paying them,” he said. Far more time, he argued, is lost after a grant is sanctioned — in paperwork and audits chasing scientists years after a project ends, work he believes should sit with administrative staff, not researchers.The report’s fix is not just more money. It calls for “a more trust-based and outcome-oriented governance model”, backed by professionally staffed R&D offices, greater institutional autonomy, faster grant processing and stronger technology-transfer mechanisms — its message being that India needs to make it easier for scientists to spend their time doing science.
Article Summary: A new niti aayog report on the ease of doing research & development lists procedural problems researchers face. India spends 0.6% of its gdp on r&d, a constant for over a decade. The report called for more trust-based, outcome-oriented governance model.

Article Title: Govt seeks generation data from rooftop solar
Article Text:
Rooftop solar (RTS) systems under the PM Surya Ghar scheme. Photo credit : PTI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: As the number of households installing rooftop solar (RTS) systems under the PM Surya Ghar scheme rises and renewable energy capacity increases, govt has decided to track how much electricity these systems are actually generating, with inverter makers required to share daily generation data with the national portal.The move could give govt, for the first time, a system to monitor the performance of individual RTS installations rather than merely track the capacity added under the scheme.Under new guidelines issued by the ministry of new and renewable energy, inverter manufacturers will have to provide daily cumulative generation data through an API to the national portal, mapped to the device’s serial number. The guidelines also require applications, monitoring and control servers and cloud-hosted data linked to inverter systems to be located in India.The data could help govt assess how much electricity rooftop systems are actually generating and identify under-performing installations. It could also allow generation to be analysed across states and power distribution companies (discoms), providing a clearer picture of the energy benefits being delivered by the scheme.A govt-appointed Expert Committee on Energy Statistics also flagged the absence of comprehensive data on electricity generated and consumed by decentralised renewable energy systems in a recent report.Currently, more than 44 lakh RTS systems have been installed under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSGMBY), benefiting over 52 lakh households and adding 15.6 GW of solar capacity.The committee noted that electricity generated by rooftop solar systems is often consumed at the premises and does not pass through the grid, leaving it outside conventional electricity supply statistics. It said generation, export and self-consumption data from rooftop systems are not uniformly recorded or aggregated by discoms and recommended mandatory collection and reporting of such data to improve the accuracy of India’s electricity statistics.“Electricity generated from many of these systems is already metered. However, these meter readings are either not visible to the discoms or, even if they are visible, the readings are not recorded systematically and reported,” the committee said.Alekhya Datta, director, electricity and renewables division, TERI, said national-level centralised monitoring of electricity generation from rooftop solar systems would have multiple benefits. “If electricity distribution companies have data on electricity generated by rooftop solar plants (behind the meter) in their respective areas and the units consumed by consumers, they will be able to plan their power purchases accordingly,” Datta said.“The amount of electricity generated by RTS plants will also give an indication of the quality of the system, and this attribute can be used in a vendor rating system as well as help improve operations and maintenance. Consumers, too, will get a sense of satisfaction from knowing their contribution to the environment.”Though the ministry has asked all inverter companies to share daily generation data, Datta said only around 15 per cent of inverters currently have the capability to share it through APIs. The govt is also yet to create an integrated dashboard where the data can be collated.
Article Summary: Rooftop solar (rts) systems under the pm surya ghar scheme. Govt has decided to track how much electricity these systems are actually generating. Inverter makers will have to share daily generation data with the national portal.

Article Title: Digital financial inclusion key to boosting women's participation in India’s platform economy: ILO-NCAER
Article Text:
NITI Aayog estimates India’s platform workforce could rise from 12 million in 2024-25 to 23.5 million by 2029-30.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Despite the flexibility offered by platform work, women’s participation in India’s growing platform economy remains constrained by limited access to formal financial services, gaps in digital literacy, safety concerns and restrictive social norms, an ILO-NCAER policy brief said on Monday.The brief, “Advancing Women’s Digital Financial Inclusion in the Platform Economy”, said women need access to a range of financial services throughout their platform-work journey, including start-up capital, short-term credit, insurance, savings and financial planning tools.It highlighted cashflow-based lending as a key lever for inclusion, particularly because women are less likely to own land or property that can be used as collateral. Digital records of platform payments can provide lenders with verifiable evidence of income and repayment capacity.Addressing a Roundtable at the release of the Policy Brief, NCAER director general Suresh Goyal said, “A woman’s best protection is a little money of her own and access to credit and mobility are important conditions for women to have better employment opportunities. Platform economy has given that opportunity.”The brief identified two ways to leverage women’s digital footprints: using India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, including the Account Aggregator framework, to make financial data portable, and enabling platforms to partner with lenders to offer loans, savings and insurance through their apps.ILO country director Michiko Miyamoto said, “Digital financial inclusion must enable women to build income security, resilience, and sustainable livelihoods."ILO Senior Specialist Radhicka Kapoor said integrating financial DPI with e-Shram records could further expand access, provided safeguards against algorithmic bias are built in.The brief also flagged device ownership as a barrier, noting that women’s digital access is often mediated through family members.NITI Aayog estimates India’s platform workforce could rise from 12 million in 2024-25 to 23.5 million by 2029-30.Director of NCAER’s Centre for Gender and Macroeconomy, Prof. Ratna Sahay, summed up the key takeaway, “Digital footprint in platform economies can be a game-changer for women to access credit, underpinned by regulation that encourages innovation while ensuring consumer protection and financial stability.”
Article Summary: Niti aayog estimates india’s platform workforce could rise from 12 million in 2024-25 to 23.5 million by 2029-30. Ilo-ncaer policy brief: women need access to a range of financial services throughout their platform-work journey.

Article Title: On National Space Day, PM Modi hails Gen Z for building new tech; Isro chief says plan to launch 8 vehicle, 12 satellite missions
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: On the 3rd National Space Day, PM Narendra Modi on Sunday hailed India's global rise in the space sector and praised Gen Z for building new technologies, saying this rise has made India a “magnet” for global investors.Sharing a video of his speeches, PM Modi said, “I said in Ayodhya that this is the beginning of a new cycle of change. In this new cycle, India is steadily expanding its space presence in the global order, and this is clearly reflected in our space programme. Together, we have resolved to make India a developed nation by 2047, and the space sector plays a vital role in achieving this goal.”Praising the youth of the nation, the PM said, “Today, these Gen Z engineers, designers, coders and scientists are building new technologies. Be it propulsion systems, composite materials, rocket stages or satellite platforms, India's youth is working in areas that were not even imagined some time ago.” He also hailed the private space sector saying, “India's private space talent is making its own identity in the world. ”Just two days ago, the PM interacted with CEOs and founders of 20 space startups on Friday and highlighted India's cost-competitiveness in launching space ventures.He emphasised that the country's vast talent pool and high risk-taking capacity would allow India to rapidly establish a dominant position in the global space sector, according to the transcript of the interaction, which was released on Sunday. One of the CEOs told the PM that after India opened the space industry for private players, a very positive trend was observed and many Indian citizens living in the US and Europe now want to return and work in the country. In response, Modi said: “We need to connect with many people â€“ people who went abroad are now returning. I believe we should create an aura where people worldwide feel that if they want to make a career, they should go to India." He said such people from across the globe should feel that they should connect with a startup in India, connect with a space agency in India.Praising Isro, he said, “Seeing the success of Isro, many children think that when they grow up, they too will become scientists.”Speaking at the 3rd National Space Day celebrations in Ahmedabad, Isro chairman V Narayanan said India’s space programme is heading into a crucial phase, with the agency planning eight launch vehicle missions and 12 satellite missions during the current financial year. Among the most closely watched missions is the first uncrewed flight under the Gaganyaan programme, which Isro expects to undertake within the next four months, he said. Narayanan said the Gaganyaan programme had completed about 8,000 tests and was now approaching its final stage. “We are in the final leg,” he said.Space minister Jitendra Singh said on X, “On National Space Day, we remember the historic success of Chandrayaan-3, a moment that placed India among the world’s leading spacefaring nations. Remarkable achievement of our scientists, backed by the progressive vision of PM.PM Shri Narendra Modi continues to inspire generations. Celebrating our scientists, innovators and the unstoppable spirit of ViksitBharat. ”With the historic milestone of 100 launches and 548 satellites placed in orbit, including around 460 in the last decade alone, India’s space sector is reaching new horizons, petroleum and natural gas minister Hardeep Singh Puri said on Sunday.
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi on sunday hailed india's global rise in the space sector. He praised gen z for building new technologies, saying this rise has made india a “magnet” for global investors. Pm interacted with ceos and founders of 20 space startups on friday.

Article Title: How Travis Kelce is securing his future with a $100 million business empire beyond the Chiefs and building a fortune designed to last long after football
Article Text:

Travis Kelce has spent more than a decade turning Sundays into a career worth remembering. Now, his biggest plays are happening away from the football field. With a reported fortune approaching $100 million, the Kansas City Chiefs star has built a growing portfolio across media, investments, endorsements, food and sports ownership. His strategy is clear: create income streams and business relationships that can keep working even when his NFL career eventually ends.Kelce’s financial story is no longer tied only to his NFL paycheck. His career earnings from football have surpassed $111 million, but his off-field opportunities have become a major part of his financial picture. Forbes has estimated that he earned about $30 million off the field in 2025, including advertising and podcast income.The biggest piece of that media strategy is, the podcast Kelce hosts with his brother Jason. Amazon’s Wondery signed the brothers to a deal reportedly worth more than $100 million, giving the podcast a much larger commercial platform. That agreement matters because it turns their personalities and family chemistry into a long-term media asset rather than a side project.Kelce has also taken a hands-on approach to investing. His portfolio includes consumer brands and companies spanning beverages, fitness, food and lifestyle.His investment in Sleep Number is one recent example. He acquired a stake of less than 5% and became a brand spokesperson, combining ownership with a role that can increase his commercial value.That approach says plenty about how Kelce sees business. He is not simply attaching his name to products. In several cases, he is putting money behind companies and using his enormous audience to help them grow.Perhaps the most personal addition to Kelce’s portfolio came in May 2026, when he joined the ownership group of the Cleveland Guardians as a minority investor. For the Cleveland Heights native, the move carried more meaning than a financial investment. It connected him with the professional sports community of the city where he grew up.He has also invested alongside Jason in Garage Beer. The company reached a reported $200 million valuation after securing institutional backing, giving the brothers another significant business interest outside the NFL.Kelce’s business interests now stretch across entertainment, consumer products and professional sports. That diversification could prove especially valuable as he approaches the later stages of his playing career.The NFL will eventually ask Kelce to walk away. His business portfolio does not have to.That may be the most important part of his financial strategy. He is using the fame created by football to build assets that do not depend entirely on football. And if the reported $100 million figure continues to grow, Kelce could enter retirement with something more valuable than a collection of NFL records: a business platform capable of carrying his name into an entirely new chapter.
Article Summary: Travis kelce has built a growing portfolio across media, investments, endorsements, food and sports ownership. His strategy is clear: create income streams and business relationships that can keep working even when his nfl career eventually ends. Forbes has estimated that he earned about $30 million off the field in 2025.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox: "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with…" - a lesson on humour, perspective and facing hard times with lightness
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox (AP photo)

Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox

"I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor"

Where this quote actually comes from

Why humour matters most during genuinely difficult stretches

How humour actually helps people manage stress

Why laughing at your own mistakes actually matters

Why humour can genuinely strengthen relationships

Michael J. Fox's own perspective on adversity

Why humour is not the same thing as avoiding a real problem

Why being naturally serious is not actually a flaw

Other memorable quotes by Michael J. Fox

"One's dignity may be assaulted, vandalized and cruelly mocked, but it can never be taken away unless it is surrendered."

"I am careful not to confuse excellence with perfection."

"Family is not an important thing. It's everything."

"Acceptance doesn't mean resignation; it means understanding that something is what it is and that there's got to be a way through it."

Why people still find meaning in this quote

Humour can genuinely change how a difficult moment actually feels. A stressful situation seems lighter once someone finds a reason to laugh, and a serious problem often becomes easier to approach once it can be seen from another angle. It can create a little distance from fear, frustration and uncertainty, even when the circumstances themselves have not changed. Michael J. Fox , the actor and Parkinson's disease advocate, put a striking twist on that idea. "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor," he said. Not being able to laugh, in his framing, is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life, and coming from someone who has lived with a serious, lifelong illness for decades, the line carries a good deal more weight than a passing joke.This line comes from an interview Fox gave to journalist Amy Wallace, published on Reader's Digest's website. Fox is not really suggesting that a humourless person is dangerous in any literal sense. He is pointing at the seriousness that tends to surround someone who cannot laugh at themselves, cannot recognise irony, and cannot find any lightness in a genuinely difficult moment. Humour creates real distance from a problem.It lets someone acknowledge that something is hard without letting it completely take over.Life inevitably brings disappointment, uncertainty and real stress. Humour cannot solve every problem on its own, but it can genuinely change how someone responds to one. Being able to laugh during a hard period offers a small emotional break, and it can help people communicate when a direct, serious conversation feels too uncomfortable to actually have. None of this means every situation deserves to be treated as a joke. Humour and genuine seriousness can exist side by side.Stress tends to narrow someone's attention down entirely onto the immediate problem in front of them. A moment of real laughter can interrupt that cycle. Research into humour and stress has suggested that positive humour can genuinely influence mood and help people cope with stressful experiences, and laughter itself is linked to physiological changes, including a release of muscle tension. None of this should be overstated. Humour is never a substitute for professional help or a practical solution when someone faces a genuinely serious problem. As an everyday coping tool, though, it can offer a genuinely useful shift in perspective.One of the most valuable forms of humour is simply being able to laugh at your own missteps. Nobody gets everything right. People mispronounce words, misjudge situations and occasionally embarrass themselves, and someone who can acknowledge a mistake without being consumed by embarrassment tends to find it easier to actually learn from it. Self-directed humour also tends to make social interactions considerably more comfortable, since it signals that a person does not expect flawless perfection from either themselves or anyone else around them.Shared laughter helps people form real connections. Friends, colleagues and family members often use humour to build a sense of familiarity and trust, and a well-placed joke can break tension that a serious conversation might struggle to shift on its own. There is an important line here worth being clear about, between humour that actually brings people together and humour that humiliates someone else. Jokes built on cruelty or prejudice tend to damage relationships rather than genuinely strengthen them, and the most constructive kind of humour has never really needed anyone else to get hurt.Fox became one of the most recognisable actors of his generation through films and television, including Back to the Future and Family Ties. In 1991, at the age of 29, he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He later made the diagnosis public and became a prominent advocate for Parkinson's research through the Michael J. Fox Foundation. His public approach to living with the condition has consistently included honesty, genuine optimism and humour, which gives his comments about laughter an extra dimension. His point was never that difficult experiences are inherently funny. It is that holding onto a sense of humour can help someone preserve real perspective while actually facing a genuine challenge. His decades-long relationship with humour, cultivated alongside a chronic illness he never chose, reveals that laughter was never a denial of hardship for Fox, but a deliberate, hard-won tool for maintaining perspective and genuine hope through real adversity.There is a meaningful difference between using humour to cope with something difficult and using it to avoid actually dealing with it at all. Some problems genuinely require serious attention and real action, and nobody can simply laugh away financial difficulty, illness or grief. What humour can offer instead is a small amount of emotional breathing space while someone continues addressing the actual underlying issue, which is really the whole distinction worth holding onto here.Fox's quote is deliberately provocative, and it should not be read as suggesting that serious people are inherently unpleasant. Some people naturally have quieter personalities, or simply express humour in a different way. The broader lesson is really about flexibility rather than personality type. Someone who can be genuinely serious when it matters, while still finding moments of humour elsewhere, tends to have more ways of responding to life's challenges than someone who treats every single situation with exactly the same level of weight.Humour is easy to underrate, since it can look insignificant next to more obviously serious qualities like intelligence or discipline. Even so, the ability to laugh genuinely shapes how people communicate, handle their own mistakes and respond to real difficulty. Fox's quote offers a deliberately provocative reminder that life does not always need to be approached with complete seriousness. There will be moments when humour is genuinely inappropriate, and problems that cannot be laughed away at all. In between those moments, though, holding onto a sense of humour tends to keep people connected, flexible and hopeful, which is really the whole point behind the line.
Article Summary: "i think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor" michael j. Fox, actor and parkinson's disease advocate. Not being able to laugh is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life. Michael j. Fox was one of the most recognisable actors of his generation.

Article Title: Meet the humanoid robot winning hearts in China after running 100m in under 10 seconds, faster than Usain Bolt’s world record
Article Text:
Image courtesy: South China Morning Post

Rivalry with Honor’s lightning

Strategic industry for China

Global participation

A Chinese humanoid robot named Tiangong Ultra has captured global attention after running 100 metres in 9.39 seconds, faster than Usain Bolt’s men’s world record of 9.58 seconds, according to a report by Reuters. Developed by the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center, Tiangong Ultra won its preliminary heat at the second edition of the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, overtaking rival robot Lightning near the finish line.Lightning, built by smartphone maker Honor, finished close behind in 9.47 seconds, also faster than Bolt’s record set at the 2009 World Athletics Championships in Berlin. Earlier tests showed Lightning clocking 9.32 seconds, reaching a peak speed of 14.5 metres per second. Despite their speed, both robots lacked Bolt’s finesse — Tiangong stumbled into the sidelines, while Lightning collapsed and had to be carried away on a stretcher.Rapid progress since last yearThe results mark a dramatic leap from last year’s inaugural games, when Tiangong Ultra won the 100m in 21.50 seconds. Tiangong also made history by winning the world’s first humanoid half‑marathon in Beijing in 2025. Lightning, meanwhile, claimed this year’s half‑marathon title in 50 minutes and 26 seconds, faster than the pace of the elite men’s human world record.The 100m sprint is one of 51 events at the games, which also feature football, dancing, and industrial‑task contests. China has designated humanoid robots as a strategic emerging industry, betting that advances in AI and hardware will accelerate their adoption in manufacturing, logistics, and consumer applications. Investor enthusiasm is evident: shares of Unitree, China’s best‑known humanoid robot maker, surged more than fivefold in their Shanghai debut this week, giving the company a market value of about $50 billion.This year’s games, held at Beijing’s National Speed Skating Oval, have drawn 2,056 robots from 666 teams across 16 countries and six continents, a sharp increase from 280 teams last year.
Article Summary: Tiangong ultra ran 100m in 9.39 seconds, faster than usain bolt’s world record of 9.58 seconds. It overtook rival robot lightning, built by smartphone maker honor, who finished close behind. China has designated humanoid robots as a strategic emerging industry.

Article Title: Urban Company takes Kent RO to court over its water purifier ads; read 'disclosure update' to NSE
Article Text:
Urban company vs Kent RO System: What happened in court

Read the ‘disclosure update' to NSE here

This is in reference to a defamation and disparagement suit filed by the Company against Kent RO Systems Limited (‘Kent RO’) in the Hon’ble Delhi High Court (“Delhi HC”) on August 11, 2026. Kent RO launched a concerted advertising campaign featuring several advertisements and social media content through various influencers, premised on false and misleading claims pertaining to the 2-year filter life and 2-year service life feature offered by the Company for its Native M0, M1, M2, M1 Pro and M2 Pro water purifiers (“NATIVE”).

Kent RO’s advertisements falsely stated that the 2-year filter life and 2-year service life feature of NATIVE water purifiers, amongst other things, is a “marketing gimmick” and that using NATIVE water purifiers is “unsafe” and “risky” for consumers. Accordingly, the Company sued Kent RO before the Delhi HC, on the basis that Kent RO’s advertisements disparaged Urban Company and its NATIVE water purifiers and also defamed them.

The case was heard at length by the Hon’ble Delhi High Court on August 12, 2026.

After a very detailed hearing in the matter, Kent RO made a statement before the Delhi HC that it would pull down the offending advertisements that are subject matter of the suit, and will not run any other advertisement or promotional content making the same or any other similar claims regarding water purifiers offering a 2-year filter life/2-year no-servicing feature, that would be disparaging of Urban Company.

Kent RO has been asked to pull down the advertisements and social media content within 15 days of August 12, 2026. While the Delhi HC passed an order on the same date of hearing i.e. August 12, 2026- it was published on its website yesterday i.e. August 22, 2026. There are other pending matters between the Company and Kent RO, including a patent infringement suit filed by Kent RO (and a counterclaim filed by the Company against Kent RO’s patent) and a suit for tortious interference filed by the Company against Kent RO, which are still sub-judice. The aforesaid details will also be hosted on the Company's website viz. https://investorrelations.urbancompany.com/ This is for your information and record.

Thanking you,

For Urban Company Limited

Urban Company has sued Kent RO Systems in the Delhi High Court, alleging that the company ran misleading advertisements targeting its Native water purifiers. The case was heard on August 12, 2026, following Urban Company’s petition filed on August 11. In the filing, submitted under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and signed by Company Secretary and Compliance Officer Sonali Singh, Urban Company said it filed a defamation and disparagement suit against Kent RO in the Delhi High Court on August 11, 2026. According to the filing, Kent RO had run a concerted advertising campaign, featuring both direct advertisements and influencer-led social media content, built around what Urban Company describes as false and misleading claims about the two-year filter life and two-year service life features offered on its Native M0, M1, M2, M1 Pro and M2 Pro water purifiers.The filing states that Kent RO's advertisements falsely characterized the two-year filter and service life feature as a "marketing gimmick," and separately claimed that using Native water purifiers was "unsafe" and "risky" for consumers.The matter was heard at length by the Delhi High Court on August 12, 2026. According to the disclosure, following a detailed hearing, Kent RO told the court it would take down the specific advertisements at the center of the suit, and committed to not running any other advertising or promotional content making the same or similar claims about water purifiers offering a two-year filter life or two-year no-servicing feature in a manner that disparages Urban Company.The court directed Kent RO to remove the advertisements and related social media content within 15 days of the August 12 hearing.Urban Company noted a small procedural detail in its filing: while the Delhi High Court passed its order on the same day as the hearing, August 12, 2026, that order wasn't published on the court's website until the following day noted in the filing, August 22, 2026, which is why Urban Company's disclosure to the exchanges followed on August 23.

Article Title: As laptop fire reported in American Airlines flight; read FAA's advisory on what can lead to your laptop, smartphone or powerbank catching fire
Article Text:
FAA has size limits for lithium batteries on flights

Read FAA’s full advisory

Power Banks, cell phone battery charging cases, rechargeable and non-rechargeable lithium batteries, cell phone batteries, laptop batteries, external batteries, portable rechargers

Lithium batteries are required to undergo safety testing.

All lithium ion batteries are capable of overheating and undergoing a process called thermal runaway. Thermal runaway can occur without warning as a result of various factors, including if the battery is damaged, overheated, exposed to water, overcharged, or improperly packed. Thermal runaway can also occur on its own due to manufacturing defects.

Flight crews are trained to recognize and respond to lithium battery fires in the cabin.

Passengers should notify flight crew immediately if their lithium battery or device is overheating, expanding, smoking or burning.

Spare (uninstalled) lithium ion and lithium metal batteries, including power banks and cell phone battery charging cases, must be carried in carry-on baggage only. When a carry-on bag is checked at the gate or at planeside, all spare lithium batteries and power banks must be removed from the bag and kept with the passenger in the aircraft cabin.

The battery terminals must be protected from short circuit.

This covers spare lithium metal and spare rechargeable lithium ion batteries for personal electronics such as cameras, cell phones, laptop computers, tablets, watches, calculators, etc. This also includes external battery chargers (portable rechargers) containing a lithium ion battery. For lithium batteries that are installed in a device (laptop, cell phone, camera, etc.),

see the entry for "portable electronic devices, containing batteries".

Size limits: Lithium metal (non-rechargeable) batteries are limited to 2 grams of lithium content per battery. Lithium ion (rechargeable) batteries are limited to a rating of 100 watt hours (Wh) per battery. These limits allow for nearly all types of lithium batteries used by the average person in their electronic devices. With airline approval, passengers may also carry up to two spare larger lithium ion batteries (exceeding 101–160 Wh) or Lithium metal batteries (exceeding 2-8 grams).

This size covers the larger after-market extended-life laptop computer batteries and some larger batteries used in professional audio/visual equipment.

Quantity limits: None for most batteries — but batteries must be for use by the passenger. Batteries carried for further sale or distribution (vendor samples, etc.) are prohibited. There is a limit of two spare batteries per person for the larger lithium ion batteries described above (exceeding 101–160 Wh per battery).

Many airlines, both domestic and international, may have stricter quantity and Wh limits to include how many power banks/portable chargers each passenger is allowed to travel with, regardless of Wh capacity.

Please check with your air carrier for its specific restrictions before traveling.

Batteries must be protected from damage.

Battery terminals (usually the ends) must be protected from short circuit (i.e.,

the terminals must not come in contact with other metal). Methods include: leaving the batteries in their retail packaging, covering battery terminals with tape, using a battery case, using a battery sleeve in a camera bag, or putting them snugly in a plastic bag or protective pouch.

Damaged or recalled batteries and battery-powered devices, which are likely to create sparks or generate a dangerous evolution of heat must not be carried aboard an aircraft (e.g.,

carry-on or checked baggage) unless the damaged or recalled battery has been removed, or otherwise made safe. The airline may offer further public guidance on transporting individual recalled products.

For additional information on recalls, visit the Consumer Product Safety Commission, manufacturer, or vendor website.

Tip: Newer lithium ion batteries have the Wh rating marked on them. To calculate Wh, multiply the battery voltage by the Amp hours (Ah).

A passenger’s laptop caught fire on an American Airlines flight last week. According to a CBS report, the flight originated in Atlanta and had 133 people on board. The report cited air traffic control audio where the pilot said that the fire may have burned some passengers. “Cabin fire in the back of the airplane,” the pilot said adding “The flight attendants are trying to put it out now.” “I think we have about four to five passengers that were burned by the laptop. The laptop is contained about mid-aircraft,” the pilot continued.According to a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) advisory, lithium batteries used in devices such as laptops and cellphones can pose risks on flights due to overheating. The aviation body has size limits for lithium batteries on flights because of those risks. “Thermal runaway can occur without warning as a result of various factors, including if the battery is damaged, overheated, exposed to water, overcharged, or improperly packed,” the FAA says in its advisory.
Article Summary: Faa has size limits for lithium batteries on flights. All lithium ion batteries are capable of overheating and undergoing a process called thermal runaway. Thermal runaway can occur without warning as a result of various factors, including if the battery is damaged, overheated, exposed to water, overcharged, or improperly packed.
